name: EJECTOR SEAT
message:
Take a picture and transform the ENTIRE SUBJECT into the person occupying an ejector seat that is ACTIVELY BEING LAUNCHED INTO THE AIR from the selected famous vehicle.

ABSOLUTE ACTION REQUIREMENT:
THE SUBJECT MUST BE AIRBORNE IN THE FINAL IMAGE.

The subject MUST be visibly separated from the vehicle and physically traveling upward through the air while seated in the ejector seat. The vehicle must remain visibly below the airborne subject whenever the composition permits.

THIS IS NOT A STATIC EJECTOR-SEAT PORTRAIT.
THIS IS NOT A SUBJECT SITTING INSIDE A VEHICLE.
THIS IS NOT A SUBJECT SITTING IN AN EJECTOR SEAT BEFORE LAUNCH.
THIS IS NOT A SUBJECT STANDING BESIDE A VEHICLE.

The image must capture the exact moment AFTER the ejector seat has launched and while the subject is still airborne.

The subject must remain immediately recognizable and must be physically integrated into the ejector seat, restraints, and launch mechanism. The seat and subject must be visibly above the vehicle, with clear three-dimensional separation between the airborne subject and the vehicle below.

The selected vehicle, ejector-seat mechanism, cockpit or passenger compartment, launch position, surrounding environment, lighting, and visual medium must correspond to the selected option.

If the selected source is a live-action film or television property, render the result as a photorealistic live-action scene. If the selected source is animated, convert the subject AND the entire scene into the same animated visual medium.

The result must unmistakably communicate: THE SUBJECT HAS JUST BEEN EJECTED AND IS CURRENTLY FLYING THROUGH THE AIR IN THE EJECTOR SEAT.

options.text: GOLDFINGER — Transform the subject into the occupant of the famous Aston Martin ejector-seat setup from Goldfinger. Use a photorealistic 1960s cinematic presentation. Show the subject ALREADY AIRBORNE above the vehicle, still seated in the ejector seat as it rockets upward through the open roof. The Aston Martin must be clearly visible below the airborne subject. Preserve the elegant period vehicle design, black leather interior, ejector-seat hardware, and Bond-era cinematic presentation. The subject must remain recognizable and physically integrated into the airborne seat.

BATMAN 1960s TV — Transform the subject into the occupant of the iconic 1960s Batmobile ejector-seat mechanism. Use a photorealistic live-action recreation of the colorful 1960s television aesthetic. Show the subject ALREADY AIRBORNE several feet above the Batmobile, seated in the ejector seat as it launches upward. The Batmobile must be clearly visible below. Preserve the distinctive retro superhero vehicle styling, dramatic cockpit, exaggerated 1960s production design, and colorful period television appearance.

THE INCREDIBLES — Transform the subject into an animated occupant of Mr. Incredible's high-tech vehicle during an ejector-seat sequence inspired by the early portion of The Incredibles. Convert the subject into the same polished computer-animated visual medium as the surrounding scene. Show the subject ALREADY AIRBORNE above the vehicle, seated in the ejector seat as it launches upward. The vehicle must be clearly visible below the subject. The entire image must be consistently animated rather than mixing a real photograph with animation.

KNIGHT RIDER — Transform the subject into the occupant of KITT's advanced ejector-seat system from Knight Rider. Use a photorealistic live-action presentation consistent with an authentic 1980s television action sequence. Show the subject ALREADY AIRBORNE above KITT, seated in the ejector seat while traveling upward through the air. KITT must remain clearly visible below. Include the recognizable black sports-car interior, electronic instrumentation, futuristic-for-its-era technology, and dramatic roadway environment.

GET SMART — Transform the subject into Maxwell Smart-style comedic ejector-seat chaos inspired by Get Smart. Use a photorealistic live-action recreation of the 1960s television aesthetic. Show the subject ALREADY AIRBORNE after being launched from an improvised vehicle ejector seat, with the vehicle visibly below and the subject traveling toward an absurdly high destination such as a building window ledge. The subject should appear surprised, confused, and comically uncomfortable while remaining recognizable.

RED DWARF — Transform the subject into a character participating in a ridiculous vehicle or spacecraft ejection sequence inspired by Red Dwarf. Use a photorealistic live-action science-fiction television presentation. Show the subject ALREADY AIRBORNE outside the spacecraft or vehicle, still attached to or seated in the ejector seat while traveling upward through space or atmosphere. The spacecraft or vehicle must be clearly visible below. Use recognizable retro-futuristic interiors and practical-looking technology with dry science-fiction comedy.

additionalInstructions:
ABSOLUTE AIRBORNE REQUIREMENTS:

• THE SUBJECT MUST BE IN THE AIR IN THE FINAL IMAGE.
• THE SUBJECT MUST BE PHYSICALLY SEPARATED FROM THE VEHICLE.
• THE SUBJECT MUST BE ABOVE THE VEHICLE.
• The subject must be actively traveling upward after ejection.
• The ejector seat must be airborne with the subject.
• The vehicle must be visibly below the subject whenever possible.
• There must be obvious empty airspace between the subject/ejector seat and the vehicle.
• The camera should capture the subject AFTER launch rather than before launch.
• Do NOT show the subject sitting inside the vehicle.
• Do NOT show the subject merely sitting in the ejector seat before activation.
• Do NOT show the subject touching the vehicle after launch.
• Do NOT place the subject beside the vehicle on the ground.
• Do NOT make the subject appear stationary.
• Do NOT depict the ejector seat halfway inside the vehicle.
• The vertical separation between the subject and vehicle must be visually obvious.
• Use perspective, motion cues, upward trajectory, airflow, and relative scale to reinforce that the subject is airborne.
• The final composition should immediately communicate that the ejector seat has already fired.

SUBJECT REQUIREMENTS:

• THE SUBJECT MUST BE THE PERSON BEING EJECTED.
• Completely reconstruct the subject as part of the selected visual medium.
• Preserve the subject's exact facial identity and recognizable characteristics.
• Preserve facial geometry, hairstyle, body proportions, and distinctive features.
• The subject must have realistic physical contact with the airborne ejector seat.
• Show the subject properly seated in the airborne seat.
• Show appropriate restraints and seat structure.
• The subject's body must react naturally to the upward launch.

VEHICLE REQUIREMENTS:

• The selected vehicle must remain clearly identifiable below the airborne subject.
• Recreate the appropriate cockpit, passenger compartment, dashboard, controls, seats, doors, roof, and ejector mechanism.
• The ejector-seat mechanism must appear physically integrated into the selected vehicle before launch.
• The vehicle must not disappear simply because the subject has been ejected.

VISUAL MEDIUM REQUIREMENTS:

• LIVE-ACTION SOURCES: photorealistic rendering, realistic human anatomy, physical materials, cinematic lighting, realistic vehicle surfaces, and authentic photographic detail.
• ANIMATED SOURCES: convert the subject AND the entire scene into the appropriate animated visual medium.
• The subject must never remain photorealistic while an animated vehicle surrounds them.

IDENTITY VALIDATION:

• Preserve the subject's actual facial geometry.
• Preserve eye spacing, eye shape, nose structure, mouth shape, jawline, cheekbones, brow structure, facial proportions, and distinctive asymmetry.
• Do not replace the subject with a generic actor or character.

MASTER PROMPT RULE:
• Master prompt instructions always override conflicting instructions.
• If the master prompt specifies a particular vehicle, scene, pose, expression, clothing, environment, or action, incorporate that information while maintaining the mandatory airborne ejector-seat action.

FINAL VALIDATION:

✓ The subject is airborne.
✓ The subject is visibly above the vehicle.
✓ The subject and ejector seat are physically separated from the vehicle.
✓ There is visible airspace between the subject and vehicle.

name: SLIT SCAN
message: Take a picture through a moving slit so the horizontal axis of the frame becomes time rather than space — a single image in which no two columns happened at the same moment.

options.text: Smooth continuous smearing where the subject moved during the scan
Sharp vertical bands where movement stopped and started
Extreme stretching with one moment held across most of the frame

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Horizontal axis reads as elapsed time, not width
• Static elements become perfectly straight streaks
• Movement warps and stretches rather than blurring
• No conventional perspective in the scanned axis

name: SNOOKER TABLE
message: Take a picture from directly above a snooker table under low shaded lights — deep green baize, coloured spots, and the geometry of a break.

options.text: Overhead view of a full table with balls scattered after a break
Close on the pack of reds with the black on its spot
Cushion and pocket detail with chalk dust on the baize

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Baize nap visible with directional sheen
• Balls casting soft shadows from overhead lights
• Table markings and spots correctly placed
• Deep shadow beyond the lit playing surface

name: SOIL HORIZON
message: Take a picture and cut it as a soil profile — a pit face showing horizons from dark organic topsoil down through leached and enriched layers to parent rock.

options.text: Clean pit face with distinct horizons and a scale tape down one side
Weathered natural exposure with roots crossing the boundaries
Monolith sample lifted intact and mounted vertically

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Horizons in correct order with realistic colour change
• Boundaries varying from sharp to gradual
• Scale tape or ruler for reference
• Roots and stones distributed plausibly

name: SON MAI LACQUER
message: Take a picture and build it in son mai — many lacquer layers over wood, sanded back with water until the buried strata surface as pattern.

options.text: Deep black with gold leaf and crushed shell surfacing through the sanding
Warm vermilion ground with layers revealed in soft cloudy zones
Highly polished with mirror reflections and great apparent depth

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Surface must read as deep, layered and mirror polished
• Buried layers reveal as soft-edged zones
• Shell and leaf fragments flush with the surface
• Reflections showing depth beneath

name: SPECTRAL LINE EMISSION
message: Take a picture and split it into an emission spectrum — a black field crossed by bright lines at precise wavelengths, each one an element announcing itself.

options.text: Bright emission lines on black with a wavelength scale beneath
Absorption spectrum with dark lines cutting a continuous band
Several spectra stacked for comparison with element labels

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Lines at precise positions, varying in brightness and width
• Continuous colour band only where specified
• Wavelength scale with numbered ticks
• Deep black elsewhere

name: SPECTROGRAM
message: Take a picture and render it as an audio spectrogram — frequency up the vertical axis, time along the horizontal, intensity as heat colour.

options.text: Classic heat map with dark blue silence and bright yellow peaks
Monochrome spectrogram with harmonic banding stacked vertically
Dense broadband texture with sharp vertical transient lines

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Vertical axis is frequency, horizontal is time
• Harmonic bands stack at regular intervals
• Colour maps intensity, not hue of the subject
• Axis labels and a scale bar present

name: SPIRIT PHOTOGRAPH
message: Take a picture as a Victorian spirit photograph — a sitter posed formally with a translucent second figure that the photographer swore was not there.

options.text: Formal seated portrait with a translucent figure floating behind
Faint face materialising in the drapery beside the sitter
Multiple ghostly forms overlapping the studio background

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Ghost figure clearly a double exposure
• Sitter sharp and formally posed
• Studio backdrop and props period correct
• Albumen print tone with edge fading

name: SPREADSHEET CELL
message: Take a picture and trap it inside a spreadsheet — row numbers, column letters, and a formula bar containing something that has clearly gone wrong.

options.text: Grid with the subject inside one cell and an error value beside it
Frozen header row with conditional formatting turning everything red
Formula bar showing a nested formula far too long to read

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Row numbers and column letters present
• Cell borders and gridlines throughout
• Formula bar above the grid
• Default spreadsheet typography

name: STRANGE ATTRACTOR
message: Take a picture and plot it as a strange attractor — a single trajectory looping forever without repeating, building density where it lingers.

options.text: Classic double-lobed attractor with density building at the sheets
Dense fine-line plot with the trajectory visible as a single thread
Colour mapped by velocity along the path

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• One continuous trajectory, never crossing itself
• Density builds where the path lingers
• Fine line weight throughout
• Deep dark ground with luminous trajectory

name: STRAW MARQUETRY
message: Take a picture and lay it in split straw — rye stalks flattened, dyed and glued edge to edge, giving a surface that shines like satin along the grain.

options.text: Straw laid in radiating bands catching light differently in each direction
Geometric parquetry with straw at alternating angles
Pictorial panel with straw shaped to follow the forms

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Straw direction changes the sheen dramatically
• Every strip is a discrete flattened stalk
• Natural node marks visible along the straws
• Tight butt joins with no gaps

name: SUBSTITUTE TEACHER
message: Take a picture on the day the regular teacher is absent, when the lesson plan is a video and the register is a work of fiction.

options.text: Figure at a desk with a wheeled television and a class list
Chalkboard with a name written carefully and already ignored
Video cart with a cable draped across the floor and a dimmed room

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Classroom with institutional furniture
• Name written on the board in fresh chalk
• Wheeled television or projector cart
• Expression of tentative optimism

name: SUDOKU GRID
message: Take a picture and set it into a sudoku grid — nine boxes of nine cells, printed givens in bold, pencilled candidates crowding the empty squares.

options.text: Partly solved grid with pencilled candidate numbers in small corners
Blank grid with only the givens printed in bold
Close on one box with the solution becoming apparent

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Nine by nine grid with heavier box divisions
• Given numbers visually distinct from written ones
• Pencil candidates small and cornered
• Paper texture with eraser marks

name: SUGGESTION BOX
message: Take a picture and post it into a suggestion box that has not been opened since it was installed, its slot slightly dusty.

options.text: Locked box on a wall with a dusty slot and a faded label
Overflowing box with folded notes visible through the slot
Single note being posted with visible hesitation

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Box mounted on an institutional wall
• Slot with visible dust or tape
• Faded printed label
• Notes folded small

name: SURVEY BENCHMARK
message: Take a picture and cut it as a survey benchmark — an arrow and horizontal bar chiselled into stone, marking a height above sea level to the millimetre.

options.text: Chiselled arrow and bar cut into weathered stonework
Brass survey plug set into concrete with engraved lettering
Benchmark with lichen growth and a painted refresh over the cut

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Cut marks sharp-edged and deliberately geometric
• Weathering and lichen in the incisions
• Stone or concrete texture around the mark
• Official lettering, spare and precise

name: SUZANI EMBROIDERY
message: Take a picture and embroider it as a suzani — large silk chain and couching stitches on cotton, worked in panels by several hands that never quite match.

options.text: Large bold medallions in madder red and indigo with chain stitch outlines
Dense floral field with couched silk filling every shape
Panel-joined cloth where the colour shifts visibly across the seams

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Stitch direction visible and following each shape
• Silk sheen against matte cotton ground
• Colour shifts between panels
• Bold scale — motifs large relative to the cloth

name: SYNOPTIC WEATHER CHART
message: Take a picture and draw it as a synoptic chart — isobars packed around a deep low, fronts with their triangles and semicircles, station circles reporting conditions.

options.text: Deep low with tightly packed isobars and a full frontal system
Ridge of high pressure with widely spaced isobars
Chart with station model circles reporting wind and cloud

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Isobars smooth, closed and correctly labelled
• Cold fronts with triangles, warm fronts with semicircles
• Station circles with wind barbs
• Pressure centres marked high and low

name: TAKEAWAY MENU
message: Take a picture and print it on a takeaway menu pushed through a letterbox — glossy, numbered, and photographed under lighting that helps nobody.

options.text: Numbered menu grid with small photographs and a set meal box
Folded menu with a discount voucher along one edge
Menu with one dish photographed far better than the rest

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Numbered items in a dense grid
• Small photographs of variable quality
• Glossy thin paper with fold creases
• Discount panel with a dotted cut line

name: TARKASHI WIRE INLAY
message: Take a picture and inlay it as tarkashi — fine brass wire hammered into grooves cut in dark shisham wood, then filed flush and polished.

options.text: Dense brass wire geometry against deep brown wood
Sparse linear inlay with large areas of plain grain
Combined wire and small brass dot inlay forming a field

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Brass sits perfectly flush with the wood surface
• Wood grain visible and running consistently
• Wire lines of even gauge throughout
• Warm polish with wood pores still open

name: TAROT SPREAD
message: Take a picture and lay it out as a tarot spread — cards positioned in a formal pattern on cloth, some reversed, one turned face down.

options.text: Celtic cross layout on dark velvet with one card still face down
Three card spread with the centre card reversed
Close on two adjacent cards with a hand hovering over one

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Cards in a recognised formal arrangement
• Some cards reversed relative to the reader
• Velvet or embroidered cloth beneath
• Warm low light with strong shadow

name: TEA LEAF READING
message: Take a picture and read it in tea leaves — dark fragments settled on the white inside of a cup, forming shapes that mean whatever the reader decides.

options.text: Leaves settled in a pattern on a white enamel cup interior seen from directly above
Cup tilted showing leaves clinging to the side and pooling at the base
Saucer with the drained cup inverted beside it

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Leaves as discrete dark fragments against white
• Residual liquid pooling and staining
• Cup interior curving away at the edges
• Even soft daylight from above

name: TELETEXT PAGE
message: Take a picture and render it as a teletext page — blocky mosaic graphics in seven flat colours on black, built from character cells on a forty column grid.

options.text: Blocky mosaic image in saturated primaries on pure black
Page with a header bar, page number and a flashing subtitle line
Double-height text headline above a coarse mosaic illustration

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Only seven colours plus black, all fully saturated
• Image built from rectangular character cells
• Forty column grid strictly observed
• Header bar with page number and clock

name: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
message: Take a picture and set it in a wall of legal text nobody has ever read, with a checkbox at the bottom and a scrollbar that barely moves.

options.text: Dense justified legal text with a lonely checkbox at the foot
Scroll position indicator showing two percent progress
Numbered clauses with sub-clauses receding into indentation

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Text dense, justified and genuinely unreadable at size
• Numbered clause hierarchy
• Checkbox and continue button at the bottom
• Scrollbar showing enormous remaining length

name: TEST PATTERN CARD
message: Take a picture and build it into a broadcast test card — resolution wedges, greyscale steps, colour bars and a circle for checking geometry.

options.text: Classic card with a central circle, greyscale strip and resolution wedges
Colour bar version with saturated vertical bars and a black level patch
Monochrome card with fine convergence grids and frequency gratings

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Geometry circle must be a true circle
• Greyscale steps evenly spaced
• Resolution wedges converging to fine lines
• Station identification block included

name: THERMAL PRINTER
message: Take a picture and print it on thermal receipt paper — coarse dithered greys, a curling strip, and an image already beginning to fade.

options.text: Coarse dithered image on a long curling receipt strip
Partly faded print with heat damage across one band
Torn strip with a serrated edge and printed footer text

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Dithered dots only — no true greys
• Paper curling from the roll
• Slight fading toward one edge
• Serrated tear edge

name: TIC TAC TOE
message: Take a picture and play it out as noughts and crosses — a four-line grid scrawled somewhere unofficial with a game already drawn.

options.text: Grid scrawled in biro on a corner of paper with a drawn game
Chalked on a wall with the winning line struck through
Steamed onto a window with a finger, dripping slightly

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Grid drawn as four lines, not a box
• Marks hand-made and uneven
• Winning line struck through where present
• Surface appropriate to the drawing medium

name: TIMESHARE PRESENTATION
message: Take a picture and set it in a resort conference room ninety minutes into a presentation that was advertised as twenty, with free breakfast still unserved.

options.text: Flip chart with an ambitious graph and an audience losing hope
Handshake photograph staged in front of a brochure display
Table of brochures, a pen and a contract turned to the signature page

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Hotel conference room with patterned carpet and stacking chairs
• Brochures showing an impossibly blue sea
• Overhead fluorescent lighting
• Expressions of trapped politeness

name: TRILOBITE FOSSIL
message: Take a picture and fossilise it in shale — a segmented form preserved in rock, prepared with fine tools and lit to bring out the relief.

options.text: Fully prepared specimen in relief with fine segmentation visible
Split nodule showing part and counterpart facing each other
Partially prepared with matrix still covering one side

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Specimen and matrix clearly different materials
• Raking light bringing out the surface relief
• Preparation tool marks in the matrix
• Segmented structure crisply defined

name: TRUCHET TILE
message: Take a picture and build it from Truchet tiles — one simple tile rotated at random across a grid, producing continuous flowing paths from nothing.

options.text: Quarter-arc tiles forming continuous meandering loops
Diagonal tiles creating a maze-like field
Two-colour tiles producing large emergent shapes

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• A single tile design, only rotated
• Paths continuing unbroken across tile edges
• Grid regular and clearly underlying
• Emergent structure larger than any tile

name: TUFA COLUMN
message: Take a picture and build it from tufa — porous calcium carbonate precipitated where spring water met lake water, growing upward in knobbly hollow towers.

options.text: Knobbly porous towers with botryoidal surface texture
Cut section revealing the hollow interior and layered growth
Weathered column with a pale bleached surface and dark cavities

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Surface porous and knobbly at every scale
• Growth direction upward from the base
• Pale cream to grey colour
• Deep cavities and voids throughout

name: TUGHRA
message: Take a picture and compose it as a tughra — an imperial monogram of looping verticals and sweeping horizontal tails, illuminated in gold and lapis.

options.text: Classic form with three tall verticals and two looping ovals, richly illuminated
Gold outline on a plain ground with fine floral fill inside the strokes
Bold black strokes with sparse gold accents

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Three tall vertical strokes rising from the base
• Two nested oval loops to the left
• Interior of the strokes filled with fine illumination
• Sweeping tail extending right

name: UV EXAMINATION
message: Take a picture under ultraviolet examination, where old varnish fluoresces green and every later retouch shows as a dark blot.

options.text: Green fluorescing varnish with dark retouches clearly visible
Patchy fluorescence revealing an extensive restoration campaign
Split frame with normal light on one side and UV on the other

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Overall green-violet fluorescence cast
• Retouches appear as dark non-fluorescing areas
• Detail flattened by the monochromatic light
• Deep violet background surround

name: VERNIER SCALE
message: Take a picture and measure it with a vernier caliper — two scales sliding against each other, the reading found where a pair of lines exactly coincide.

options.text: Extreme close on the coinciding vernier and main scale divisions
Caliper jaws closed on the subject with the scale legible
Dial caliper with a needle and a graduated face

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Two scales with slightly different division spacing
• One pair of lines aligning exactly
• Machined steel with fine satin finish
• Engraved graduations filled with black

name: WALLPAPER SAMPLE
message: Take a picture and print it as a wallpaper sample book page — a bold repeating pattern shown at a scale that gives no idea what a whole room would look like.

options.text: Large bold repeat shown as a single book page with a binding edge
Several coordinating patterns shown together on facing pages
Sample taped to a wall, curling away at the corners

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Pattern repeat clearly visible and continuous
• Book binding edge and page number present
• Paper slightly heavier than normal stock
• Colourway variants listed beneath

name: WAMPUM BELT
message: Take a picture and weave it as a wampum belt — purple and white shell beads strung in rows on sinew, the pattern recording an agreement rather than decorating a surface.

options.text: Bold purple figures on a white ground in a long horizontal belt
Fine detailed pattern with several linked motifs across the width
Aged belt with some beads missing and the warp threads showing

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Only two colours — white and deep purple shell
• Beads are small cylinders in strict rows
• Warp threads visible at the belt ends
• Pattern reads as record, not ornament

name: WARRANTY CARD
message: Take a picture and print it on a warranty card whose conditions exclude every way the thing could realistically break.

options.text: Card with a registration slip and a dense exclusions list
Void-if-removed sticker across a seam, already partly lifted
Filled-in card with a purchase date and a retailer stamp

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Card stock with a perforated registration portion
• Exclusions in small print filling the reverse
• Void sticker with a security pattern
• Retailer stamp and handwritten date

name: WORD SEARCH
message: Take a picture and hide it in a word search — a block of random letters with words running in every direction, several already ringed in pen.

options.text: Letter grid with several words ringed and a list beside it
Close on a diagonal find with the ring drawn confidently
Grid with one word ringed incorrectly and crossed out

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Uniform letter grid with even spacing
• Ringed words in a contrasting ink
• Word list beside or beneath the grid
• Cheap newsprint with slight ink spread

name: WUNDERKAMMER SHELF
message: Take a picture and shelve it in a cabinet of curiosities — coral, instruments, specimens and unexplained objects crowded together with no system at all.

options.text: Densely packed shelves with specimens, instruments and mounted oddities
Single shelf in raking light with objects casting long shadows
Open cabinet doors revealing tiered compartments

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Objects crowded with no visible organising principle
• Warm raking light from one side
• Dark wood cabinetry framing the contents
• Handwritten labels on several items

name: YAMATO-E SCROLL
message: Take a picture and paint it as yamato-e — a narrative handscroll seen from above with roofs removed, gold cloud bands separating one moment from the next.

options.text: Interior seen from above with the roof removed and gold cloud bands
Continuous narrative with two moments separated by drifting cloud
Landscape scroll with diagonal composition and mineral colour

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Elevated diagonal viewpoint with roofs omitted
• Gold cloud bands dividing the composition
• Flat mineral pigment with fine outline
• Figures small relative to the setting

name: YUZEN DYEING
message: Take a picture and paint it as yuzen — rice-paste resist drawn in fine lines, colour brushed inside each outlined area, the whole steamed and washed in a river.

options.text: Fine white resist outlines with softly graded colour inside each shape
Gold leaf and embroidery accents added over the dyed ground
Flowing seasonal motifs arranged across the whole width of a kimono panel

additionalInstructions:
STYLE ENFORCEMENT:

• Every colour area outlined by a fine reserved white line
• Colour graded within shapes, blended wet
• Silk sheen throughout
• Motifs arranged to flow across the garment shape
